This appeal coming on for admission this da

 Order

This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is filed by the insurance company being aggrieved of award dated 22.04.2019 passed by the learned Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal to the First Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal (M.P.) in claim case case No.562/2018 on the ground that accident took place between a motorcycle and a scooty.

entities.text: Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: First Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Appellant is insurer of the motorcycle bearing registration No. MP38-S-1931.
2.

It is submitted that accident had taken place head on and, therefore, aspect of contributory negligence should have been considered and award should have been appropriated between the owner, driver of the scooty and motorcycle.
3. Shri Shiv Kumar Sharma, learned counsel for the respondents, in his turn, submits that firstly there is no evidence to prove the aspect of contributory negligence.

Secondly, death occurred in relation to the occupant of the motorcycle and not of the driver, therefore, in the light of law laid down by the Supreme Court in Khenyai Vs. New India Assurance Company Ltd., (2015) 9 SCC 273,
claimant can recover compensation from either of the joint tortfeasors, namely, owner, driver and insurer of the motorcycle or and from the owner, driver of the scooty.

entities.text: Khenyai Vs. New India Assurance Company Ltd., (2015) 9 SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Therefore, in the light of law laid down by the Supreme Court in Khenyei (supra), I do not find any illegality in the impugned award calling for interference, inasmuch as, deceased was not responsible for the accident and therefore, the appeal fails and is dismissed.
